root_cause.text: A race in KVM x86 posted-interrupt synchronization let __kvm_apic_update_irr() trust PID.ON and return early with *max_irr = -1 when PIR had already been consumed, because it failed to rescan the LAPIC IRR for already-pending interrupts.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly says the bug is caused by a race between vmx_sync_pir_to_irr() and __vmx_deliver_posted_interrupt(), where PID.ON can be set after PIR was harvested, leading to a second sync with “pi_test_on() -> TRUE” but “PIR empty” and “*max_irr = -1, early return, IRR NOT SCANNED”; the patch fixes this by changing __kvm_apic_update_irr() to call apic_find_highest_vector(regs + APIC_IRR) when pi_harvest_pir() finds PIR empty.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message explicitly says the bug is caused by a race between vmx_sync_pir_to_irr() and __vmx_deliver_posted_interrupt(), where PID.ON can be set after PIR was harvested, leading to a second sync with “pi_test_on() -> TRUE” but “PIR empty” and “*max_irr = -1, early return, IRR NOT SCANNED”; the patch fixes this by changing __kvm_apic_update_irr() to call apic_find_highest_vector(regs + APIC_IRR) when pi_harvest_pir() finds PIR empty.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix __kvm_apic_update_irr() to report the current highest IRR vector when no PIR entries are harvested before returning false.
intent_record.what: The code moves the pi_harvest_pir(pir, pir_vals) check to occur before initializing max_updated_irr and *max_irr, and adds a new failure path that sets *max_irr to apic_find_highest_vector(regs + APIC_IRR) before returning false when pi_harvest_pir() yields no harvested PIR data.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when no PIR bits are harvested, the function now updates *max_irr to reflect the highest pending vector already present in the APIC IRR instead of leaving it at -1 or unchanged, which preserves correct interrupt state reporting while still indicating that no new PIR data was applied.

grouping_result.intent: Fix __kvm_apic_update_irr() to report the current highest IRR vector when no PIR entries are harvested before returning false.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the root cause in __kvm_apic_update_irr(): instead of returning early with an invalid/no IRR state when no PIR entries are harvested, it reports the current highest IRR vector, addressing the missed LAPIC IRR rescan/race condition described.

candidates.rationale: This conditional is the key early-exit gate that trusts the posted-interrupt state. When harvesting finds no PIR entries, the function takes the false return path without rescanning LAPIC IRR, enabling the race where interrupts were already consumed from PIR but remain pending in IRR.
This early return embodies the bug: it exits with *max_irr still set to -1 when PIR has already been consumed, instead of reporting the current highest pending vector from LAPIC IRR.
Initializing *max_irr to -1 becomes vulnerable in combination with the early return path, because the function can return this stale value without checking LAPIC IRR for already-pending interrupts.

vuln_statements.explanation: This early return is the direct vulnerable statement. When no PIR entries are harvested due to the posted-interrupt synchronization race, the function exits immediately and leaves the caller with the previously initialized *max_irr value, without rescanning the LAPIC IRR for interrupts that were already consumed from PIR but are still pending.

This condition is the buggy gate that trusts the posted-interrupt state alone. In the race window, pi_harvest_pir() can report no PIR bits even though interrupts are already pending in LAPIC IRR, causing the function to take the incorrect early-exit path.

This initialization becomes part of the vulnerability because the later early return can propagate -1 to the caller without updating it from the LAPIC IRR state, masking already-pending interrupts after PIR has been consumed.
